excerpt: Batanes Red is a registered garlic variety. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council in 2017 as NSIC 2017 Gr 02. It takes about 150 days from planting to harvest, with 8,440 kilograms per hectare on average in the trials.

blocks.text: Key facts about Batanes Red garlic
How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

Batanes Red garlic takes about 150 days from planting to harvest. That is 36.3 days longer than the average of the 7 garlic varieties with a day count, 113.7 days. A shorter crop frees the field sooner and dodges more of the weather, while a longer one often fills more.

Its average yield of 8,440 kg/ha beats the average of its group, 5817.14. It sits in the top quarter of its group. Trial yields come from well managed plots, so your own will depend on water, fertilizer, pests and timing. Its seller gives about 150 days after planting.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.

blocks.text: It showed no weak spot in the ratings on record. Still, a resistant variety can break down when a new strain or pest population comes, so keep scouting. Read up on [purple blotch of onion](/diseases/purple-blotch), [thrips](/pests/thrips).

The pests and diseases that hit garlic fields most often: [Cercospora leaf spot](/diseases/cercospora-leaf-spot), [cutworm](/pests/cutworm), [Fusarium wilt](/diseases/fusarium-wilt), [onion armyworm](/pests/onion-armyworm), [purple blotch of onion](/diseases/purple-blotch). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Yield:** 8.44 t/ha on raised beds, 6.70 t/ha with minimum tillage.
**Fruit:** Rhomboid bulb with a prominent base plate, violet cloves and violet outer skin.
**Season:** Dry season, needs cool, windy weather during the growing period.
Moderately resistant to purple blotch, Cercospora leaf spot and Fusarium bulb rot.
Only slight thrips, leaf folder and mite damage in the NSIC trials.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: registered with NSIC in 2017, the highest raised bed yield among the seven NSIC garlic entries, but the slowest to mature. Check these against what farmers near you have seen, because the same variety can do differently from one town to the next.
Where and when to plant Batanes Red garlic

It is recommended for the dry season. Native Ilocos garlic is small but strong in flavor and keeps well. Plant cloves from a clean, local source after the rains, because garlic needs the cool, dry months. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng gulay](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-gulay).

items.q: How long does it take to harvest?
items.a: It takes about 150 days from planting to harvest. Then the weather and your care decide the exact day.
The record shows 8,440 kilograms per hectare on average in the trials. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of Batanes Red?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
